# Surefire groups for the Build workflow.
#
# Format: a group starts with a line "[<label>]"; the lines after it, up to the next
# "[<label>]" line, hold its Surefire -Dtest patterns, separated by commas, spaces or line
# breaks. Lines starting with '#' are comments.
#   label    words of lower-case letters and digits separated by single spaces or '-', at
#            most 25 characters. It names the job, "test (jdk 21, <label>)", so say what
#            the group tests. Its id, the label with '-' for every space ("run-approval"),
#            names the surefire-reports artifact and is the argument of "verify".
#   pattern  matched against the simple class name; only letters, digits, '_' and '*' are
#            allowed. Either a prefix ("Grant*Test") or one class name.
#
# Groups are features, by test class name. Estimated class time per group, from the
# per-class times of Build runs 37871680943 and 37871413114 (mean of their JDK 21 and 25
# jobs, 21,500 s in total; class times in a job that forks one JVM per core run higher
# than in the old single-job run):
#   run approval and mail      53 classes  ~4,460 s
#   activation and reruns      37 classes  ~3,750 s
#   windows and audit history  57 classes  ~4,090 s
#   items and storage          40 classes  ~3,230 s  (ItemIdentityBindingTest, ~480 s)
#   authorization and plugins  53 classes  ~3,070 s  (AuthorizationEntryGuardTest, ~370 s)
#   parameters and ui          37 classes  ~2,910 s
# ItemIdentityBindingTest and AuthorizationEntryGuardTest are the two slowest classes.
# The first-letter shards these replaced measured, on the same runs: A ~2,270 s,
# B-F ~2,630 s, G-L ~4,310 s, M-P ~3,120 s, Q-R ~4,980 s, S-Z ~4,210 s.
#
# .github/scripts/test-shards.py check fails the workflow when a test class matches no
# group or more than one group, when a group matches no class and when a pattern matches
# no class (left behind by a rename or a deletion). A new test class whose name starts like
# the classes of one group needs no change here if that group has its prefix; otherwise add
# the prefix or the class name to the group of the feature it tests. Rebalance (move a
# family to another group, or split a feature into two descriptively labelled groups) when
# one group grows much slower than the others.
